$comment: Generated by scripts/sync-remote-tools.ts from teros-remote packages/mca/tools.json (daemon 0.8.0) — do not edit by hand.

tools.name: health-check
tools.description: Internal health check. Verifies that every allowed root is accessible and reports which search engine (ripgrep or the in-process fallback) is active.

tools.name: list-roots
tools.description: List the roots this machine exposes (the daemon's allowedRoots). Useful for auditing scope when a path is rejected with FORBIDDEN.

tools.name: read-file
tools.description: Read a text file with optional line-based pagination. Returns content formatted as "cat -n" (numbered lines) plus metadata (name, size, lineCount, kind). Use offset+limit for ranges or head/tail for the first/last N lines. Returns text content; binary files are rejected.

head.description: Return only the first N lines (overrides offset/limit)

tail.description: Return only the last N lines (overrides offset/limit)

includeRaw.description: If true, include raw content (without line numbers) in addition to formatted

tools.name: read-files
tools.description: Read multiple text files in a single call. Returns an array with one entry per requested path (ok, content/error). Each file is read with the same default limits as `read-file`; pass perFileLimit to override. Failures on individual paths do not abort the batch.

tools.name: read-binary
tools.description: Read a binary file (image, PDF, audio, archive, …) and return base64 + detected MIME type. For text files use `read-file`. Hard cap 10 MB to avoid blowing up the chat context.

tools.name: create-file
tools.description: Write content to a file, overwriting if it exists. Safety: an existing file must have been read first in this session (use `read-file` before overwriting). For new files, parent directories are created automatically. Use `edit-file` for in-place modifications and `append-file` for additions.

tools.name: append-file
tools.description: Append content to the end of a file. Creates the file (and parents) if it does not exist. Does NOT require a prior read (appends are non-destructive to existing content). For replacing content, use `create-file` (after `read-file`) or `edit-file`.

tools.name: edit-file
tools.description: Replace exact string occurrence(s) in a file. By default fails if `oldString` appears zero or multiple times — pass `replaceAll: true` to rewrite every match. The replacement is literal (no regex). Returns a unified diff of the change. For structured hunks use `patch-file`; for larger rewrites use `create-file`.

filePath.description: Path to the file to edit

dryRun.description: Preview the change (returns diff without writing). Default false

tools.name: patch-file
tools.description: Apply a unified diff (patch format) to a file atomically. Useful for multi-hunk fixes where several edits must go together. Uses fuzzy matching (fuzzFactor 2) so minor context drift is tolerated. Returns whether all hunks applied. For single-point changes prefer `edit-file`.

filePath.description: Path to the target file to patch

dryRun.description: Preview the patch (returns diff without writing). Default false

tools.name: list-files
tools.description: List directory entries with metadata (name, type, size, mtime, kind). Optionally recursive via `depth`. Honors `ignore` patterns (glob-style) and `respectGitignore`. Paginates with `limit` + `cursor`. For a hierarchical view use `tree-view`; for pattern-based search use `find-files`.

path.description: Directory to list (default: the first allowed root)

depth.description: Max recursion depth (0 = current dir only, default 0, max 20)

respectGitignore.description: If true, honor .gitignore from the listed directory

tools.name: tree-view
tools.description: Return a hierarchical JSON tree of a directory up to `depth` levels. Files have size and mtime; directories have children. Honors `ignore` patterns and `respectGitignore`. Capped by maxNodes to prevent runaway output. Use `list-files` for flat pagination or `find-files` for pattern match.

path.description: Root directory (default: the first allowed root)

tools.name: file-info
tools.description: Return metadata for a single path: exists, type (file/directory), size, mtime, permissions. Does NOT read content. Prefer this over `read-file` when you only need to check existence or size.

path.description: Path to the file or directory (e.g. '/workspace/docs')

tools.name: hash-file
tools.description: Compute the cryptographic hash of a file (default sha256). Reads the file and hashes in memory. Useful for integrity checks and detecting changes between reads.

tools.name: find-files
tools.description: Find files matching a glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}"). Results sorted by mtime (most recently modified first). Honors `ignore` patterns and `respectGitignore`. Use `search-in-files` for content search and `list-files` for flat directory listing.

path.description: Base directory (default: the first allowed root)

tools.name: search-in-files
tools.description: Search file contents for a regex pattern using ripgrep. `output_mode` controls the shape: "content" returns {file, line, match, context} objects; "files" returns one entry per matching file with matchCount; "count" returns only totals. Supports context lines (-B/-A), include glob, case insensitive, multiline. Shell-injection safe (args are not interpolated). For finding files by name use `find-files`.

pattern.description: Regex pattern (Rust regex syntax via ripgrep)

path.description: Base directory or file (default: the first allowed root)

contextBefore.description: Lines of context before each match

contextAfter.description: Lines of context after each match

type.description: Pre-defined file type filter passed to ripgrep --type (e.g. js, py, rust, ts, go, md). Faster than `include` when you target a known language

multiline.description: Allow pattern to match across newlines

limit.description: Max matches or files to return (default 50, max 100)

tools.name: delete-file
tools.description: Delete a file or directory. Set `recursive: true` for non-empty directories. Idempotent: succeeds silently if the path does not exist (reports existed=false).

path.description: Path to the file or directory to delete (e.g. '/workspace/old-dir')

tools.name: copy-file
tools.description: Copy a file or directory. For directories set `recursive: true`. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite: true`. Parent directories of the destination are created automatically.

source.description: Path to the source file or directory (e.g. '/workspace/docs')

tools.name: move-file
tools.description: Move or rename a file or directory. Fails if the destination exists unless `overwrite: true`. Parent directories of the destination are created automatically.

source.description: Path to the source file or directory

tools.name: create-directory
tools.description: Create a directory. By default creates parent directories as needed (recursive). Idempotent: returns created=false if the directory already exists.

path.description: Path to the directory to create (e.g. '/workspace/docs')

tools.name: device-status
tools.description: Report the paired machine's daemon status: online/offline, uptime, daemon version, allowed roots, whether bash is enabled, and the last tunnel error.

tools.name: get-info
tools.description: Get system information about the paired machine: identity (name, hostname, deviceId, daemon version), OS/arch/kernel, system uptime and boot time, local and external IP addresses (external is best-effort and may be null), CPU/memory/root-disk totals, battery status when present, and the daemon's scope (allowed roots, exec enabled). Read-only, no arguments.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command on this machine. Scope: full access as user <daemon-user> — NOT limited to the allowed roots (<allowedRoots>). Returns stdout, stderr and exit code. `cwd` defaults to the first allowed root as a convenience for relative paths; it is not a boundary.

description.description: ALWAYS provide this: a 5-10 word description of what the command does. It is shown to the user as the tool-call title.

cwd.description: Working directory (default: the first allowed root)

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds (default 120000, max 600000). On expiry the process group is killed and partial output is returned with error TIMEOUT.

stream.description: Accepted for parity with mca.teros.bash; streaming is not available over the tunnel in v1

tools.name: pull-file
tools.description: Pull a single file FROM this machine INTO the workspace volume, over the dedicated transfer plane (chunked ~512KB, sha256-verified end-to-end, resumable by offset after a reconnect). The path must be inside the allowed roots. The result is metadata only (bytes, sha256, duration, destination) — file content never appears in the tool result. Use `mode: "resume"` with the returned resumeToken to continue an interrupted transfer.

filePath.description: Absolute path on this machine (must be inside an allowed root)

destinationPath.description: Destination path in the workspace volume (e.g. /workspace/downloads/file.bin). Defaults to /workspace/<basename>.

mode.description: create (fail if destination exists) | overwrite | resume (continue from the last acked offset; requires resumeToken)

resumeToken.description: Token from a previous interrupted transfer of the same file (mode "resume")

tools.name: push-file
tools.description: Push a single file FROM the workspace volume TO this machine, over the dedicated transfer plane (chunked ~512KB, sha256-verified end-to-end, resumable by offset after a reconnect). The destination path must be inside the allowed roots. The result is metadata only (bytes, sha256, duration, destination) — file content never appears in the tool result. Use `mode: "resume"` with the returned resumeToken to continue an interrupted transfer.

filePath.description: Destination path on this machine (must be inside an allowed root)

sourcePath.description: Source path in the workspace volume (e.g. /workspace/uploads/file.bin)

size.description: Total size in bytes (hint from the backend; -1 when unknown)

mode.description: create (fail if destination exists) | overwrite | resume (continue from the last acked offset; requires resumeToken)

resumeToken.description: Token from a previous interrupted transfer of the same file (mode "resume")

tools.name: manifest-directory
tools.description: List a directory tree on this machine as a manifest: every regular file with { relPath, size, mtime, sha256 }. Read-only; the path must be inside the allowed roots. Safety caps (transfer.maxManifestFiles / maxManifestBytes) abort with LIMIT_EXCEEDED on very large trees.

directoryPath.description: Absolute path on this machine (must be inside an allowed root)

tools.name: pull-directory
tools.description: Pull a directory tree FROM this machine INTO the workspace volume. Builds a manifest first ({ relPath, size, mtime, sha256 } per file), then transfers the files one by one over the dedicated transfer plane (chunked, sha256-verified). Files whose destination hash already matches are skipped (resume after an interrupted run). Per-file errors are reported at the end without aborting the batch. The result is metadata only — file content never appears in the tool result.

directoryPath.description: Absolute source path on this machine (must be inside an allowed root)

destinationPath.description: Destination directory in the workspace volume (e.g. /workspace/downloads/project). Created as needed.

tools.name: push-directory
tools.description: Push a directory tree FROM the workspace volume TO this machine. Fetches the volume manifest first, then receives the files one by one over the dedicated transfer plane (chunked, sha256-verified). Files whose local hash already matches are skipped (resume after an interrupted run). Per-file errors are reported at the end without aborting the batch. The result is metadata only — file content never appears in the tool result.

sourcePath.description: Source directory in the workspace volume (e.g. /workspace/builds/release)

directoryPath.description: Absolute destination path on this machine (must be inside an allowed root)

tools.name: sync-directory
tools.description: Synchronize a directory tree between this machine and the workspace volume (rsync-lite, no rsync on either side). With `dryRun: true` it only computes the diff: `added` (in source, not in destination), `changed` (size/mtime candidates confirmed by sha256), `deleted` (in destination, not in source). With `dryRun: false` it transfers ONLY the delta over the dedicated transfer plane. Deletions are NEVER applied unless `delete: true` is passed explicitly — by default they are reported and left untouched. `direction` picks the source side: "pull" (machine → volume) or "push" (volume → machine). The result is metadata only.

direction.description: pull = machine is the source (sync INTO the volume); push = volume is the source (sync ONTO this machine)

directoryPath.description: Directory on this machine (must be inside an allowed root)

dryRun.description: true (default) = compute and report the diff only; false = apply the delta

delete.description: Allow deletions on the destination when applying (default false — deleted files are only reported)
